sample_unit: clinical notes (50,000 Mount Sinai ED notes plus 500 MIMIC-IV discharge notes)

links.outcome: Prevalence of stigmatizing, judgmental, discrediting, stereotyping language in clinical notes
links.effect: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of MIMIC-IV notes; elevated odds with substance use presentations (aOR 3.09) and frequent utilization (aOR 2.85).
links.quote: Biased language appeared in 6.5% (3229 of 50,000) of Mount Sinai notes and 7.4% (37 of 500) of Medical Information Mart for Intensive Care IV notes.

unlisted_practices: Using an LLM to detect and rewrite biased or stigmatizing language in clinician documentation
Identifying modifiable contributors to biased documentation (shift timing, provider type, utilization)

screen.reason: Evaluates GPT-4's performance retrospectively in detecting and suggesting revisions for biased clinical notes, but does not test an organizational deployment practice or safeguard comparison.
